Naomi / Ben —

Thanks for the forward. I reviewed Crestline_DPA_Redlines_v3 and logged our comments in Legal_DPA_commentlog.pdf (attached). High-level position and next steps below.

Summary position (two parallel tracks):
1) Standard position (recommended): Accept their SCCs request and sign an addendum that references the current EU Commission SCCs (post-2021 set) + our standard Transfer Addendum that documents the limited export paths (EU -> US). We will:
   - Maintain a declared hosting footprint of EU + US (US only where customer explicitly opts in via Order Form).
   - Add an explicit clause: cross-border transfers outside the EU/US require a tailored agreement (Transfer Addendum) and prior notice.

2) Customer-preferred (soft opt): If Crestline insists on an EU-only contractual guarantee, offer EU-only hosting as a priced option (one-time onboarding + monthly surcharge). This avoids broader export risk and is operationally feasible for dedicated capacity.

Legal redline highlights (see attached comment log):
- Roles: we accept Controller/Processor split as-is, but we need explicit subprocessor onboarding and a 30-day notice for any new subprocessor that handles EU personal data.
- SCCs: we will accept the EU Commission SCCs but must preserve our liability and warranty caps; Crestline's redline deleted our limitation — put that back.
- Incident response: tighten SLA for breach notification to 72 hours for incidents affecting EU personal data (they redlined to 7 days).
- Export tools: require that any export exception be documented via a numbered Transfer Addendum that lists the routes, subprocessors, and legal basis.

Evidence requested for procurement/security review (please collect these and send to me):
- Current subprocessor roster (documents names, location, purpose).
- Hosting region map (regions where their tenant would be deployed) and whether those regions are on dedicated pools.
- SOC 2 scope statement + most recent report (if we can share summary).
- KMS/Encryption whitepaper or short summary (key management controls, BYOK availability).

Timing: I can turn our clean counter + tracked changes by EOD tomorrow (2029-04-05) if we get the evidence above by EOD today. If Crestline needs an EU-only position before then, we'll prepare the priced EU-only addendum language as an alternative.

Attachments: Legal_DPA_commentlog.pdf

Irene Choi
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
